knownAsymmetry: ONNX export is QInt8-quantized with a declared 512-token cap; :8081 GGUF is unquantized with a 2048-token cap. All sampled texts are well under 512 tokens so capacity does not confound this run. IMPORTANT CORRECTION (post-hoc, after seeing the result): quantization alone does NOT explain what was observed. A QInt8-vs-unquantized gap would show high (~0.95+) but imperfect cosine agreement -- what was actually measured is a UNIFORM near-zero band (-0.086 to +0.090) across all 32 rows with no outliers and no high-agreement rows, which is the signature of a structural representation mismatch, not a precision difference. Do not cite this quantization note as an explanation for the NOT_ADMITTED result below.

structuralChecksPerformed: ONNX model output tensor: confirmed 'last_hidden_state', shape [1, seq, 768] -- matches onnx-embed.ts's pooling indexing math exactly (t*768+d for a [1,seq,hidden] row-major layout). Verified live via a direct session.run() probe, not assumed.
Tokenization: confirmed real, plausible SentencePiece subword token IDs for a sample text (not empty, not all-UNK, not garbage).

config.json: architectures=['Gemma3TextModel'], use_bidirectional_attention=true, hidden_size=768, head_dim=256 -- consistent with EmbeddingGemma's documented architecture, not a wrong/mismatched checkpoint shape.

Pooling strategy: both sides configured for mean pooling -- :8081 via launch-embed-server.ps1's --pooling mean flag, onnx-embed.ts via explicit mean-pool-over-attention-mask code. Not a mean-vs-last-token mismatch as far as configuration goes.

tokenizerParityCheck.method: Directly compared llama.cpp's :8081 POST /tokenize endpoint against the ONNX export's AutoTokenizer (transformers.js) for 3 real sample texts.

results.text: Postgres is the canonical source of truth

tokenizerParityCheck.verdict: EXACT MATCH, 3/3 -- llama.cpp's internal tokenizer and the ONNX export's tokenizer.json produce IDENTICAL token IDs for identical text (ONNX wraps the same content-token sequence in BOS=2/EOS=1, which :8081's /tokenize output omits but the embedding call presumably adds internally -- consistent, not a discrepancy). The original 'leading hypothesis' (tokenizer/vocab mismatch) is DEFINITIVELY RULED OUT, not merely unconfirmed.

explicitlyRuledOut: QInt8 quantization precision gap alone (would show high not near-zero cosine)
Empty or degenerate tokenization (confirmed real subword IDs)
Tokenizer/vocabulary mismatch (confirmed IDENTICAL token IDs across 3 real texts via direct comparison against :8081's own /tokenize endpoint)
rootCauseInvestigation.remainingLeadingHypothesis: SUPERSEDED by a direct, decisive follow-up test -- see withinExecutorSemanticSanityCheck below. The attention-masking hypothesis above was reasonable given the evidence at the time but was not the most direct test available; a self-consistency check localized the fault to a specific side before that hypothesis needed to be pursued.

withinExecutorSemanticSanityCheck.method: Instead of comparing the two executors against EACH OTHER (which can't distinguish 'both broken differently' from 'one broken, one healthy'), embedded 2 semantically-similar text pairs and 2 semantically-dissimilar text pairs through EACH EXECUTOR INDEPENDENTLY, and checked whether that executor's own cosine scores separate similar from dissimilar content. A healthy executor should show a real gap; a broken one should not.

8081_gguf_cuda.discriminationGap: ~0.30 (similar pairs clearly, meaningfully higher than dissimilar pairs)
8081_gguf_cuda.verdict: HEALTHY -- confirms :8081 is semantically discriminative on its own, independent of the ONNX comparison. This is the executor already proven live for taxonomy retrieval earlier this session.

onnx_cpu_1.29.0.discriminationGap: ~0.04 (similar and dissimilar pairs nearly indistinguishable, all compressed into a narrow 0.88-0.94 band)
onnx_cpu_1.29.0.verdict: UNHEALTHY -- classic embedding-space anisotropy/collapse signature: all embeddings cluster in a narrow high-cosine cone regardless of actual semantic content, a well-documented failure mode of naive post-training quantization (QInt8 here) applied to mean-pooled transformer embeddings without calibration.

withinExecutorSemanticSanityCheck.conclusion: DECISIVE: the fault is on the ONNX side, not the :8081/GGUF side. :8081 is independently confirmed semantically healthy. ONNX's own embeddings fail to discriminate similar from dissimilar text even in isolation -- this is not merely 'disagreement between two valid executors', it is evidence that the ONNX QInt8 export itself produces degenerate embeddings.
withinExecutorSemanticSanityCheck.correctionToEarlierReasoning: The report originally dismissed QInt8 quantization as an explanation for the near-zero CROSS-executor cosine, reasoning that quantization alone would produce high-but-imperfect agreement rather than near-zero. That reasoning about cross-executor correlation was not wrong, but it missed the real mechanism: quantization-induced WITHIN-executor anisotropy (embeddings collapsing into a narrow, low-discrimination cone) is exactly what this follow-up test measured directly, and that alone is sufficient to explain near-zero cross-executor cosine -- a semantically-spread healthy space (:8081) compared against a collapsed narrow cone (ONNX QInt8) will look uncorrelated even though the collapse, not a tokenizer or architecture bug, is the actual root cause. The attention-masking hypothesis is no longer the leading explanation and was not needed to resolve this.

conclusion: NOT_ADMITTED — worst-case cosine -0.0860 is below the 0.85 admission floor; ONNX output does not yet reliably agree with the proven :8081 executor for at least one input.
